title: Butterfly
subtitle: Commitment requires accepting embarrassment
sourceCredit: Rob Carr · The Moth Radio Hour, “Acceptance”

shot.title: The visible field
shot.direction: A student stands on the open field, overly aware of a distant fraternity house.
shot.soundDirection: Wind on grass, sneakers, airy wing flutters and a delighted exhale.

illustration.direction: On an open grassy soccer field under soft daylight, the acting student stands rigid with arms close to his sides and toes planted too carefully. A fraternity house sits far beyond the field edge, no identifiable people in its windows. The teacher waits a few paces away, ordinary-sized and relaxed. His wary eyes go toward the distant building while open grass gives his inhibited body too much exposure. Preserve believable perspective and actual distance across the field.

shot.title: A teacher’s hand
shot.direction: One small hand demonstration begins in stepped movement.
shot.soundDirection: Wind on grass, sneakers, airy wing flutters and a delighted exhale.

illustration.direction: The teacher demonstrates a small butterfly-like arm movement with naturally bent elbows, one wrist softly raised and the other lower, knees loose and feet grounded in grass. Her expression is earnest, not polished or mocking. The student watches from the same few paces away, shoulders still tight. The distant house remains visible but does not become a looming fantasy monster. Arms remain complete human arms; the gesture supplies all the wings needed.

illustration.direction: The student turns his head from the distant house back to the teacher, one hand half-raised in an embarrassed question while the other hangs tensely. The teacher has stopped demonstrating and stands patiently with open hands low beside her body, leaving him room to decide. Both full bodies share the same field ground plane. shot.title: The first stiff flap
shot.direction: His arms begin at uneven angles, embarrassingly small.
shot.soundDirection: Wind on grass, sneakers, airy wing flutters and a delighted exhale.

illustration.direction: The student attempts a tiny uneven flap, elbows held awkwardly away from his ribs and hands bent as he takes a cautious short step. His torso is still stiff, sneakers contact the grass naturally and the arms remain visibly joined at both shoulders. The teacher watches without laughing, a few paces behind. The smallness of the motion and his concentrated face make embarrassment legible without turning his body into a caricature.

actions.direction: One awkward effort: his right forearm begins, the left catches up, and the shoulders follow. The grounded lower body stays quiet; this is a tentative flap rather than a looping flight.

beats.caption: Well... then I’d better have wings.
beats.speaker: STUDENT

shot.title: Then wings
shot.direction: He opens his shoulders and commits his body to the exercise.
shot.soundDirection: Wind on grass, sneakers, airy wing flutters and a delighted exhale.

illustration.direction: The student now opens his shoulders and makes a broad, asymmetrical sweep of both human arms while stepping into the open field, one heel lifting and the other foot bearing weight. His face shows effort and a surprised emerging smile. The teacher remains behind near their starting point, watching supportively. Grass bends under actual shoes; no floating body, costume wings or magic butterflies. The distant house is smaller in the composition because his action has taken attention.

actions.direction: The actor’s head and chest open before the forearms follow with different timing. His wrists finish the arc softly, then both arms return through a quiet hold. The teacher and ground stay fixed.

beats.caption: I think I forgot who was watching.

shot.title: Who was watching
shot.direction: He realizes his attention has shifted while still in motion.
shot.soundDirection: Wind on grass, sneakers, airy wing flutters and a delighted exhale.

illustration.direction: The student has crossed a real modest stretch of the soccer field, seen in a wider lateral view with the teacher much farther behind.
